translations.text: Then those men were bound, still wearing their clothes, their caps, and what was fastened to their feet, and were thrown into the middle of the blazing fiery furnace.
Because the king's command prevailed, the furnace was heated extremely hot.
And these three, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the middle of the blazing furnace. And they walked in the middle of the flame, singing praises to God and giving glory to the Lord.
Azariah stood there and prayed in this way. He opened his mouth in the middle of the fire and said:
“You are blessed, Lord, God of our fathers. You are blessed, and your name is glorious forever.
For you are righteous in everything you have done. All your works are true, all your ways are straight, and all your judgments are true.

And the judgments you have carried out concerning everything you have brought upon us and upon [?], the city of our fathers, are true. For in truth and justice you have brought all these things upon us because of our sins.
For we have sinned and acted lawlessly; we have turned away from you.
We have sinned in everything, and we have not obeyed your commandments, nor kept them, nor carried them out as you commanded us, so that things might go well for us.
Everything you have brought upon us and everything you have done to us, you have done in justice and truth.
You handed us over to lawless enemies, apostates, and to a king who is oppressive and more wicked than anyone on the whole earth.
Now, therefore, we cannot open our mouths, because shame and disgrace have come upon your servants and those who worship you. [?]
[?] all.
You are blessed in the temple of your holy glory. You are blessed and glorious forever.
You are blessed, you who look down upon the depths, who sit upon the cherubim. You are blessed and exalted forever.
You are blessed upon the throne of your kingdom. You are blessed and exalted forever.
You are blessed in the vault of heaven. You are blessed and honored forever.
All the works of the Lord, bless the Lord. Bless him and exalt him forever.
Heavens, bless the Lord. Bless him and exalt him forever.
Angels of the Lord, bless the Lord. Bless him and exalt him forever.
All the waters above heaven, bless the Lord. Bless him and exalt him forever.
All the powers of the Lord, bless the Lord. Bless him and exalt him forever.
Sun and moon, bless the Lord. Bless the Lord and exalt him forever.
Stars of heaven, bless the Lord; bless him and exalt him forever. …

I, Daniel, saw in a vision at night. I kept watching until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days was seated. His clothing was white like snow, and the hair of his head was like pure wool. His throne was a flame of fire, and its wheels were blazing fire.
A river of fire flowed out before him. Thousands upon thousands served him, and tens of thousands upon tens of thousands stood before him. The judge sat down and opened books.

I was watching at that moment, and I heard loud voices speaking words that the horn was uttering. I kept watching until the beast was killed, its body was destroyed, and it was given to the fire to be burned.
And the rule and authority of the beasts were brought to an end, but they were granted life for a time and a season.
I was watching in the night vision, and there was someone like a son of man coming on the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and came into his presence.
He gave him dominion, authority, and kingship, and all the peoples, tribes, and languages served him. His authority endured forever and ever, without end, and his kingdom was indestructible.
I was troubled in my soul, and the visions in my head shook violently. I, Daniel, when I saw these things in my vision while sleeping, [?]
[?] was troubled and fell facedown on the ground. He touched me and made me stand on my feet.
He said, “Look, I will tell you what will happen at the end of the wrath, for the vision concerns the end of a period of time.
The ram you saw with the horns is the king of the Persians and the Medes.
The male goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
As for the horn that broke and the four horns that rose in its place, they are four kings who will arise from his nation, but not with his power.
At the end of their reign, when their sins have reached their full measure, a king with a shameless face will arise, one who understands riddles.
His power will be strong, but not through his own power. He will cause astonishing destruction, prosper, and act, and he will destroy the strong among the holy people.

The yoke of his collar will prosper, with deceit in his hand. His heart will become proud, and he will destroy many through deceit. He will stand over the destruction of many and break them with his hands like eggs.
The vision of evening and morning that was spoken is true. But you must seal the vision, because it concerns many days from now.”
I, Daniel, slept and became exhausted. Then I rose and carried out the king’s business. I was amazed by the vision, and no one understood it.
In the first year of Darius, the son of Ahasuerus, of Median descent, who became king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years in the word of the Lord that had come to Jeremiah the prophet: seventy years for the completion of Jerusalem’s desolation.
I turned my face toward the Lord God to seek him with prayer and supplication, with fasting and ashes.
I prayed to the Lord my God and confessed, saying, “Lord, great and wonderful God, you keep your covenant and your mercy for those who love you and keep your commandments.
We have sinned, acted unjustly, broken the law, and rebelled. We have turned away from your commandments and your judgments.
We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our rulers, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to you, Lord, but shame belongs to us, as it does today—to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, those nearby and those far away, in every land where you scattered them because of the disobedience they committed against you, Lord.
Shame belongs to us, our kings, our rulers, and our ancestors, because we have sinned.
Compassion and forgiveness belong to you, Lord our God, because we have rebelled against you.
We have not obeyed the voice of the Lord our God by walking according to his law, which he set before us through his servants the prophets.

And all [?] transgressed your law and turned away, refusing to listen to your voice. The curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, came down upon us because we sinned against him.

He has fulfilled the words he spoke against us and against the judges who judged us, bringing great calamities upon us. Nowhere under the whole heaven have such things happened as those that happened in Jerusalem.
As it is written in the law of Moses, all these calamities have come upon us. Yet we have not pleaded before the Lord our God to turn away from our unjust deeds and to understand every truth.
The Lord our God watched over our wickedness and brought these things upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all the deeds he has done, and we have not obeyed his voice.
Now, then, Lord our God, you who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself that remains to this day, we have sinned and acted lawlessly.

Lord, in all your mercy, let your anger and your wrath turn away from [?], your holy mountain. For we have sinned, and because of our wrongdoing and that of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become an object of reproach among all those around us.
Now, then, Lord God, listen to the prayer of your servant and his pleas, and reveal your face over your holy place, which lies desolate, for your own sake, Lord.

My God, incline your ear and listen. Open your eyes and see our destruction and the destruction of your city, over which your name has been invoked. For we do not present our pleas for mercy before you on the basis of our own righteousness, but on the basis of your abundant mercy, Lord.
Hear us, Lord! Forgive us, Lord! Pay attention, Lord! Act for your own sake, and do not delay, my God, because your name has been proclaimed over your city and over your people.
I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sins and the sins of my people, [?], and presenting my plea before the Lord my God concerning the holy mountain of my God.
While I was still speaking in my prayer, look! The man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the first vision, came flying and touched me at about the time of the evening sacrifice.
He instructed me and spoke with me, saying, “Daniel, I have now come out to teach you understanding.”
At the beginning of your plea, the word went out, and I have come to tell you, because you are a dearly loved man. Consider the word and understand the revelation.

Seventy weeks have been decreed for your people and for the holy city, to bring sin to an end, to seal up our sins, to blot out our wrongdoings and forgive wrongdoings, to bring everlasting righteousness, to seal up the vision and a prophet, and to anoint the holy of holies.

You will know and understand: from the issuing of the word to restore and rebuild [?] until the ruler, the anointed one, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will return, and the square and the outer wall will be rebuilt, and the times will become empty.

After the sixty-two weeks, the anointing will be blotted out, and judgment will come upon him that is not empty. He will destroy the city and the holy place along with the ruler who is coming, and cut them off in a flood, and leave them until the end of the war that has been decreed amid destruction.
In the third year of Cyrus, [?]
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, that is, the Tigris, [?].
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a man dressed in linen, with his waist girded with gold from Uphaz.
His body was like beryl, his face looked like lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and feet were like polished bronze, and the sound of his words was like the sound of a crowd.
I, Daniel, alone saw this revelation. The men who were with me did not see it, but great terror fell upon them, and they fled in fear.
But I was left alone and saw this great revelation. No strength remained in me; my glory [?] turned to ruin, and I could not retain any strength.
I heard the sound of his words, and I was distressed as I heard him. I fell with my face to the ground.
Then a hand touched me and raised me onto my knees.

He said to me, “Daniel, you are a greatly beloved man. Understand these words that I am saying to you, and stand on your feet, for I have now been sent to you.” When he said these words to me, I stood up trembling.
